chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about two moneychangers who bought silver with dinars. One of them said to his companion, "Pay on my behalf," while he was well-off, and if he wished to pay, he would pay, so his companion paid on his behalf. Then it occurred to him to buy his companion's share with a profit. Is that valid?
He عليه السلام said: "There is no harm in it."

key_terms.بِدَنَانِيرَ: with dinars, i.e. gold currency used as payment
key_terms.بِرِبْحٍ: with a profit added in the subsequent purchase
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no legal objection to it; it is permissible
key_terms.مُوسِرٌ: financially able and not incapable of payment
key_terms.نَصِيبَ: the partner's share or portion in the purchase
key_terms.وَرِقًا: silver coinage or silver currency being purchased
key_terms.ٱنْقُدْ: pay in cash or settle the amount

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for one partner in a currency exchange deal to buy the other partner’s share at a profit after paying on his behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a transaction between two moneychangers involving shared purchase and one partner paying on behalf of the other. It indicates that if one later buys the other's share with a profit, the transaction is permissible. The report is relevant to rulings on exchange, partnership, and commercial dealings.
